hook_text: Muddy water goes into this marsh at one end and comes out clear at the other. How?
clip_script: The wetland at Wakkerstroom. Reeds, sedges, crowned cranes and frogs. Muddy water flows in. The plants slow it down, so the mud settles. Roots and stems filter it, and plants and bacteria take in some dissolved substances. Clearer water flows out! And in a storm, the wetland soaks up water like a sponge, then lets it out slowly all through the dry season. Protect our wetlands!
visual_style: Whiteboard wetland with brown water entering one side, reeds in the middle and blue water leaving, then a sponge soaking up and dripping.
mood: Calm and green, like a quiet morning in the reeds.
pacing: Muddy in, clear out, then the sponge squeeze.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out if there is a wetland near your home.
